scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the central Travancore region of Kerala, specifically associated with the Pulaya, Kurava, and Paraya communities.
It is historically and culturally linked to the agricultural practices of paddy cultivation.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is a ritual performance representing the stages of paddy cultivation, serving as a cultural expression of the agricultural labor performed by the Pulaya, Kurava, and Paraya communities.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves a group of eight men and a group of women.
The men begin by ploughing the field and planting seedlings.
The women join later, bringing breakfast and assisting with the planting.
on_screen: Formation: The dance takes place in a paddy field with participants moving through stages of cultivation.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is performed to the accompaniment of the harmonium, idakka, and tabla.
Listen for the harmonium, idakka, tabla.
The music is driven by the combination of the harmonium, the traditional idakka drum, and the tabla, providing a rhythmic accompaniment to the agricultural narrative.
